messages:
Sam: Heads-up — bank POC hit a blocker. They can stream but their proxy requires short-lived creds + signed callback URL. Need a quick pattern we can hand them.
Leila: ok. do they expect websocket or SSE?
Sam: they prefer websocket for binary safety, but will accept SSE. main constraint is corporate proxy that only allows outbound HTTPS with mTLS to specific hosts.
Leila: got it. two viable approaches: 1) outbound webhook (Redwood sends to their callback_url) with signed URL + HMAC header; 2) client-initiated streaming over websocket/WSS with short-lived tokens (recommended for interactive).
Leila: sample Node snippet for client-initiated WSS with short-lived creds:
```
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?token=eyJ...');
ws.on('open', () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({input: 'hi'})));
ws.on('message', (msg) => console.log(msg));
```
Sam: can we support their mTLS requirement? they currently terminate at a corporate proxy that requires client certs.
Leila: for Private/Dedicated yes — we can put the instance inside their VPC or allow an edge gateway that supports mTLS to the proxy. For Hosted, we can't accept arbitrary mTLS client certs to our multi-tenant edge.
Jordan: pricing note: if they want persistent websocket connections at 200 concurrent users, estimate Dedicated reserved capacity. Rough calc: 2x concurrency headroom, plan for 400 streams, ~N GPUs depending on model. I can draft numbers.
Maria: security questionnaire — they asked about key management and audit logs. We support KMS integration (customer-managed KMS) and per-request audit events in Console. Also we can provide IP allowlist + SSO (SAML) for the admin plane.
Sam: do we have a quick template answer for the "callback signing" control? they need proof we can rotate keys and produce verifiable HMACs.
Leila: yes — we have an Ops-runbook snippet. Example signing header: `X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=BASE64(HMAC(secret, payload))`. Rotate secret via KMS and publish public key thumbprint in the integration manifest.
Sam: perfect. can we also return structured output (they want a strict JSON schema per message for downstream ingestion)?
Leila: yes — use Structured Output v2. We can enforce a schema and reject nonconforming completions or emit a parse-safe wrapper. For streaming, we emit JSON fragments like: `{"part":1, "chunk":"..."}` and a final `{"__redwood_done":true, "result": {...}}`.
Sam: any code for function/tool-calling pattern? they want Redwood to call their internal service when model invokes a tool.
Leila: recommended: use `tool_call` events with callback_url. Example event payload we POST to their endpoint when model chooses a tool: `{ "tool": "lookup_account", "args": {"acct_id":"123"}, "request_id": "r-..." }`. Attach `X-Redwood-Signature`. If they can't accept inbound, we can poll a webhook queue or let the client proxy the tool calls.
Jordan: timeline — presales deck + runbook by EOW, pricing ballpark in 24h, SSO/KMS answers in the questionnaire doc. I'll own the pricing calc.
Maria: I'll fill the security spreadsheet: SOC2 status (yes), penetration test cadence (annual), data residency options (EU/US region, Private for on-prem).
pre-sales-bot: Reference docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/presales/streaming-handshake and https://redwood.ai/docs/security/integration-checklist :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks team. Next steps: 1) share Node + Python short-lived token examples w/ bank; 2) Jordan to post Dedicated estimate; 3) Maria to update sec spreadsheet. I'll loop in their IAM engineer tomorrow.
Leila: ping me if they need a proxy config example (nginx sidecar or envoy). I can paste a minimal envoy filter for signed callback verification.
Sam: sweet. closing this thread after we share artifacts. :rocket:
